Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
29 September 2026 .
Brent $ 102.33 -3.14 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 The Maritime Executive reports a Kuwaiti tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz; Lloyd's List names it as a KOTC vessel.

02 Brent stood at $102.33, down 3.14%, as of 20:57 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 Scripps News reports negotiations between the US and Iran continue after the US rejected Iran's latest proposal to open the Strait of Hormuz.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains a live combat zone. The Maritime Executive reports a Kuwaiti tanker was struck in the strait, with Lloyd's List naming the vessel as a KOTC tanker; the attacker has not been identified in this feed. gCaptain reports the maritime picture is hardening to read, with delayed disclosure of vessel strikes raising questions about how much of the fighting is going unreported. On the diplomatic track, Scripps News reports negotiations between the US and Iran continue after the US rejected Iran's latest proposal to open the Strait of Hormuz; KREM reports Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the strait. Iran's position, per the background, is that it will not soften its terms. On throughput, IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $102.33, down 3.14%, as of 20:57 UTC. The site's 24-hour event index shows 48 indexed developments in the last 24 hours. As of 20:50 UTC, 232 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
